text:
Support Lead: FYI we just got an escalated ticket from Acadia (high volume customer) — they say p95/p99 latency jumped ~3x around 2026-03-12 18:00 UTC. They attached dashboard screenshots and a few request IDs. They're hitting /v1/generate primarily.

Alex G: copying the screenshots into the thread — looks like our hosted-api p95 on the frontend dashboard went from ~220ms to ~700ms. p99 looks worse. Error rate is flat, 5xxs are negligible.

Maria C: any recent deploys around that time?

Deploy Bot: deploy completed: api-service v2.13.4 -> v2.14.0 by jamal at 2026-03-12T17:58:30Z :rocket:

Jamal S: that was a small change — removed a deprecated exporter wrapper and bumped prometheus-client lib. Nothing that touches the runtime path afaik.

Tina K: interesting — support sent a CSV of request durations. Their breakdown shows a cluster of requests in 500-1000ms bucket starting ~18:00. Do we have raw histograms for redwood_request_duration_seconds?

Observability Bot: historic metric available: redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate"} series retained 90d.

Alex G: I suspect this is a metrics calculation mismatch. Our dashboard uses a pre-aggregated p95 gauge (we started emitting it last year), while the support CSV was computed from raw request logs using direct percentile. If the exporter change altered bucket boundaries or the way summaries are aggregated we'll see divergence.

Maria C: can you check promql? what query is the dashboard using now?

Alex G: Dashboard query (current):
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket{env="prod",route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (le))
```
But we also have an emitted metric: redwood_request_p95_seconds{route="/v1/generate"}. The dashboard was switched to the histogram-based query last month for better accuracy, but maybe the exporter change broke bucket alignment.

Jamal S: the prometheus-client bump flattened floating point bucket labels from "0.005" to "0.005000" in some builds. Should be equivalent, but if our rollup job was doing string-based joins it could mis-aggregate. I pushed a patch to the exporter last week (PR #451) that changed default buckets to an HDR-like set for faster quantile approximations.

Tina K: ah — changing default buckets is a red flag. If the client now emits different 'le' boundaries, histogram_quantile will compute different results. Is there a way to confirm bucket sets pre/post deploy?

Observability Bot: recent sample of distinct 'le' values for redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket: ["0.001","0.005","0.01","0.025","0.05","0.1","0.25","0.5","1","2.5","5","10"] at 17:50 UTC; and ["0.0005","0.0025","0.01","0.04","0.1","0.3","0.8","2","4","8","16"] at 18:05 UTC.

Support Lead: that's a pretty clear difference — customer saw latency jump exactly after the deploy time. They want a mitigation now.

Maria C: immediate mitigations: 1) revert exporter change (if safe), 2) temporarily switch dashboard to use emitted redwood_request_p95_seconds gauge (if that metric is still backed by old logic), 3) for the customer route, route traffic to dedicated pool or older model variant. Which is quickest?

Jamal S: revert is possible but needs code + canary roll. I can trigger an emergency revert to v2.13.4 which would replace exporter changes.

Alex G: switching dashboard to use emitted p95 gauge is fastest for ops/visibility. Query: `max_over_time(redwood_request_p95_seconds{route="/v1/generate",env="prod"}[10m])` — gives near-instant readwing. But need to confirm that gauge isn't also impacted by the exporter bump.

Tina K: Support asked for a reproducible test. Steps I suggested:
1) curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <test-token>" -H "X-Request-ID: local-repro-<n>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"token test"}'
2) repeat ~100 requests at varying concurrency (ab)
3) capture response times and compare to metrics in Prometheus for those request-ids (logs contain request-id).

Jamal S: I'll run a quick canary revert in us-east-1 and watch the p95 for /v1/generate. If it drops back then we have a smoking gun.

Observability Bot: canary revert job started: revert/api-service-to-v2.13.4 in us-east-1 at 2026-03-12T19:08:20Z.

Alex G: also opened a promql diff to compare histogram_quantile vs emitted gauge over time:
```
# histogram quantile
hq = histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (le))
# emitted gauge
g = max_over_time(redwood_request_p95_seconds{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])
# test query
hq - g
```
If we see large positive delta after 18:00 it's the bucket change.

Tina K: I ran that diff for the last 4 hours in the dev cluster and saw deltas ~0 before 17:58 and ~+450ms between 18:00-18:30.

Support Lead: customer is asking for ETA on fix and if we will credit them. They reported user impact.

Maria C: next steps / timeline:
- Jamal: finish canary revert and confirm metric realignment (target: 30m)
- Alex: if revert proves the cause, update dashboards to fallback to emitted p95 gauge until we standardize buckets across services (target: 1-2h)
- Tina: provide repro steps + dataset to support for credit evaluation (target: 1h)
- SRE: we should add an alert for sudden histogram 'le' set changes across releases to catch this automatically.

Jamal S: canary revert result: us-east-1 revert succeeded at 2026-03-12T19:12:08Z. p95 on canary group dropped from ~710ms -> ~230ms within 2 scrape intervals. Rolling revert to global initiated.

Observability Bot: global rollback completed at 2026-03-12T19:25:30Z.

Alex G: confirmed — the histogram_quantile vs emitted gauge delta closed after rollback. This is definitely exporter bucket change.

Maria C: long-term fix: enforce normalized bucket sets across all exporters (config / code), and for safety, don't change bucket defaults without a major/compatibility note. Also consider emitting canonical p95 gauges from runtime using HDR histograms (less sensitive to bucket labels).

Tina K: messaging for the customer: we rolled back the change; p95 has returned to baseline; we're adding a guard to prevent this class of metric drift. Draft response: "We identified a metrics bucket change introduced in a recent minor deploy that affected percentile calculations in our dashboards. We have rolled back the change, latency returned to baseline, and we're adding deploy safeguards. We're offering a credit for the observed degradation — DM me for details." :white_check_mark:

Support Lead: perfect. I'll send that and keep the ticket open until we add the alert.

Jamal S: followups: create PR to pin bucket config and add unit test that verifies histogram 'le' set doesn't change unintentionally. I'll own it.

Alex G: I'll add dashboard fallback and a grafana annotation for the deploy that caused it so we have a visible audit.

Tina K: I'll close the repro steps loop with support and attach the CSV + my local test script.

Support Lead: thanks team. Great triage. :tada:
